claim: Human ESCs/iPSCs represent a primed pluripotent state corresponding to the post-implantation epiblast.
source: Human ESCs/iPSCs represent a primed pluripotent state corresponding to the post-implantation epiblast; while mouse ESCs/iPSCs represent a naïve state of pluripotency found in the pre-implantation blastocyst stage (Brons et al., 2007; Huang et al., 2014; Tesar et al., 2007; Ware, 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior research establishing this distinction between human and mouse pluripotent states.

claim: Mouse ESCs/iPSCs represent a naïve state of pluripotency found in the pre-implantation blastocyst stage.
source: Human ESCs/iPSCs represent a primed pluripotent state corresponding to the post-implantation epiblast; while mouse ESCs/iPSCs represent a naïve state of pluripotency found in the pre-implantation blastocyst stage (Brons et al., 2007; Huang et al., 2014; Tesar et al., 2007; Ware, 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior research establishing this distinction between human and mouse pluripotent states.

claim: The 5iLAF culture system allows the establishment of naïve pluripotency in different types of human cells, including cells from pre-implantation embryos, primed pluripotent stem cells, and somatic cells.
source: The widely used 5iLAF culture system allows the establishment of naïve pluripotency in different types of human cells, including cells from pre-implantation embryos, primed pluripotent stem cells, and even somatic cells (Pastor et al., 2016; Theunissen et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research demonstrating the versatility of the 5iLAF system.

claim: Secondary human inducible fibroblast-like cells (2° hiF) showed significantly decreased proliferation ability with long-term culturing and passaging.
source: Consistent with previous observations (Cacchiarelli et al., 2015), the 2° hiFs showed significantly decreased proliferation ability and naïve reprogramming efficiency, as well as increased senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity with long-term culturing and passaging (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D)
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D and citation to prior work.

claim: Secondary human inducible fibroblast-like cells (2° hiF) showed significantly decreased naïve reprogramming efficiency with long-term culturing and passaging.
source: Consistent with previous observations (Cacchiarelli et al., 2015), the 2° hiFs showed significantly decreased proliferation ability and naïve reprogramming efficiency, as well as increased senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity with long-term culturing and passaging (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D)
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D and citation to prior work.

claim: Secondary human inducible fibroblast-like cells (2° hiF) showed increased senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity with long-term culturing and passaging.
source: Consistent with previous observations (Cacchiarelli et al., 2015), the 2° hiFs showed significantly decreased proliferation ability and naïve reprogramming efficiency, as well as increased senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity with long-term culturing and passaging (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D)
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D and citation to prior work.

claim: The decreased proliferation ability, naïve reprogramming efficiency, and increased senescence of 2° hiFs were rescued by immortalizing the cell lines with constitutive human TERT expression.
source: these effects were rescued by immortalizing the 2° hiF cell lines (2° hiF-T) with constitutive human TERT expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D demonstrating rescue of phenotypes.

claim: Morphological changes occurred in hiF-T cells at approximately day 2 upon dox treatment.
source: Upon dox treatment, morphological changes occurred in hiF-T cells at approximately day 2, and small cell aggregates were observed as early as day 6 (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by observations shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Small cell aggregates were observed as early as day 6 during naïve reprogramming.
source: Upon dox treatment, morphological changes occurred in hiF-T cells at approximately day 2, and small cell aggregates were observed as early as day 6 (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by observations shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Dome-shaped colonies emerged and expanded after the culture conditions were changed from conventional hESC medium to 5iLAF medium on day 6.
source: Dome-shaped colonies emerged and expanded after the culture conditions were changed from conventional hESC medium (hESM) to 5iLAF medium on day 6 (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by observations shown in Figure 1A.

claim: GFP+ colonies were observed at day 20 of naïve induction using the OCT4-ΔPE-GFP reporter system.
source: GFP+ colonies were observed at day 20 of induction (Figure 1B) and were increased during the reprogramming process (Figure 1B)
evidence: Supported by observations shown in Figure 1B.

claim: GFP+ colonies increased during the naïve reprogramming process.
source: GFP+ colonies were observed at day 20 of induction (Figure 1B) and were increased during the reprogramming process (Figure 1B)
evidence: Supported by observations shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Approximately 91.4% of clonally derived niPSC-Ts were GFP+ as detected by FACS analysis.
source: reaching ~91.4% in clonally derived niPSC-Ts, as detected by FACS analysis (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by FACS data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Derived niPSC-Ts exhibited robust expression of core pluripotency markers OCT4, SOX2, NANOG and TRA-1–60.
source: Immunostaining results of the derived niPSC-Ts exhibited robust expression of core pluripotency markers (OCT4, SOX2, NANOG and TRA-1–60) and naïve pluripotency markers (DPPA3 and UTF1) (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Derived niPSC-Ts exhibited robust expression of naïve pluripotency markers DPPA3 and UTF1.
source: Immunostaining results of the derived niPSC-Ts exhibited robust expression of core pluripotency markers (OCT4, SOX2, NANOG and TRA-1–60) and naïve pluripotency markers (DPPA3 and UTF1) (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Almost all niPSC-Ts were negative for SSEA-3 and SSEA-4 expression.
source: In agreement with recent reports (Pastor et al., 2016), almost all niPSC-Ts were negative for SSEA-3 and SSEA-4 expression (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1D and citation to prior work.

claim: Pearson correlation distance analysis of mRNAs segregated the cell samples into three distinct categories including hiF-T/0d/2d/6d, 8d/12d and 14d/20d/24d+dox/24d-dox/niPSC-T.
source: The Pearson correlation distance analysis of mRNAs segregated the cell samples into three distinct categories including hiF-T/0d/2d/6d, 8d/12d and 14d/20d/24d+dox/24d-dox/niPSC-T (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: MDS analysis exhibited a continuous trajectory of transcriptional dynamics from hiF-Ts to established niPSC-Ts.
source: multi-dimensional scaling (MDS) analysis exhibited a continuous trajectory of transcriptional dynamics from hiF-Ts to established niPSC-Ts (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by MDS analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The cellular states at days 20–24 during naïve reprogramming were similar.
source: However, distinct from the results for the primed reprogramming system (Cacchiarelli et al., 2015), the cellular states at days 20–24 during naïve reprogramming were similar, and dox withdrawal did not result in dramatic transcriptional changes in the cells on day 24 (Figure 2B)
evidence: Supported by MDS analysis shown in Figure 2B and comparison to prior work.

claim: Dox withdrawal did not result in dramatic transcriptional changes in the cells on day 24 during naïve reprogramming.
source: However, distinct from the results for the primed reprogramming system (Cacchiarelli et al., 2015), the cellular states at days 20–24 during naïve reprogramming were similar, and dox withdrawal did not result in dramatic transcriptional changes in the cells on day 24 (Figure 2B)
evidence: Supported by MDS analysis shown in Figure 2B and comparison to prior work.

claim: Epiblast-specific markers representing naïve pluripotency were gradually up-regulated during the naïve pluripotency induction process.
source: Compared with those in the primed reprogramming system, the epiblast-specific markers representing naïve pluripotency were gradually up-regulated (one-tailed t-test p-value=5.99e-22), whereas the primed-specific genes were gradually down-regulated (one-tailed t-test p-value=1.67e-3) during the naïve pluripotency induction process (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis (p-value=5.99e-22) and data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Primed-specific genes were gradually down-regulated during the naïve pluripotency induction process.
source: Compared with those in the primed reprogramming system, the epiblast-specific markers representing naïve pluripotency were gradually up-regulated (one-tailed t-test p-value=5.99e-22), whereas the primed-specific genes were gradually down-regulated (one-tailed t-test p-value=1.67e-3) during the naïve pluripotency induction process (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis (p-value=1.67e-3) and data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Transcriptional factors OTX2 and ZIC2 showed transient up-regulation followed by marked down-regulation during naïve reprogramming.
source: We also observed transient up-regulation followed by marked down-regulation of transcriptional factors OTX2 and ZIC2 during naïve reprogramming, which were known to direct OCT4 to primed state-specific enhancer sites (Buecker et al., 2014) and exhibited robust activation during primed reprogramming (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and citation to prior work on OTX2 and ZIC2 function.

claim: OTX2 and ZIC2 direct OCT4 to primed state-specific enhancer sites.
source: We also observed transient up-regulation followed by marked down-regulation of transcriptional factors OTX2 and ZIC2 during naïve reprogramming, which were known to direct OCT4 to primed state-specific enhancer sites (Buecker et al., 2014) and exhibited robust activation during primed reprogramming (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research (Buecker et al., 2014).

claim: The activation of OSKM down-regulated genes involved in cell junction and extracellular matrix organization occurred in two waves, at day 12 and day 20 of naïve reprogramming.
source: The activation of OSKM down-regulated genes involved in cell junction and extracellular matrix (ECM) organization occurred in two waves, at day 12 and day 20 of naïve reprogramming (Figure 2C; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pluripotency-associated gene networks were activated in two waves during naïve reprogramming.
source: More importantly, pluripotency-associated gene networks were also activated in two waves; the earlier one consisted of genes with an early embryogenesis signature such as gradual up-regulation of CDH1 and NANOG from day 2, whereas the later one comprised genes with pre-implantation characteristics, such as DPPA3 and TFCP2L1 (Figure 2C; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The earlier wave of pluripotency-associated gene network activation consisted of genes with an early embryogenesis signature such as CDH1 and NANOG.
source: More importantly, pluripotency-associated gene networks were also activated in two waves; the earlier one consisted of genes with an early embryogenesis signature such as gradual up-regulation of CDH1 and NANOG from day 2, whereas the later one comprised genes with pre-implantation characteristics, such as DPPA3 and TFCP2L1 (Figure 2C; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The later wave of pluripotency-associated gene network activation comprised genes with pre-implantation characteristics, such as DPPA3 and TFCP2L1.
source: More importantly, pluripotency-associated gene networks were also activated in two waves; the earlier one consisted of genes with an early embryogenesis signature such as gradual up-regulation of CDH1 and NANOG from day 2, whereas the later one comprised genes with pre-implantation characteristics, such as DPPA3 and TFCP2L1 (Figure 2C; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The first transient wave of gene expression peaked at day eight and was enriched in genes characteristic of late embryogenesis and pattern specification, such as LHX9 and the HOX cluster genes.
source: For the transiently up-regulated genes during naïve reprogramming, the first transient wave peaked at day eight and was enriched in genes characteristic of late embryogenesis and pattern specification, such as LHX9 and the HOX cluster genes (Figure 2C; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The second transient wave of gene expression peaked around day 12–14 and included metabolism-associated genes, such as IGF2 and AFP.
source: The second wave peaked around day 12–14 and included metabolism-associated genes, such as IGF2 and AFP (Figure 2C; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The third transient wave of gene expression peaked during the late reprogramming process at approximately day 24 and was enriched in genes important for gamete generation and sexual reproduction, such as OVOL1 and CGB5.
source: The third wave, which peaked during the late reprogramming process at approximately day 24, was enriched in genes important for gamete generation (Fisher's exact test p-value=1.934e-3) and sexual reproduction (Fisher's exact test p-value=3.517e-3), such as OVOL1 and CGB5 (Figure 2C; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis (p-values) and data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The gene expression program with pre-implantation-like signatures exhibited significantly different dynamics in naïve compared with primed reprogramming systems.
source: Notably, the gene expression program with pre-implantation-like signatures exhibited significantly different dynamics in naïve compared with primed reprogramming systems, which exhibited robust up-regulation along the naïve reprogramming process, peaking in niPSC-Ts (Figure 2C, D).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2C and 2D comparing naïve and primed systems.

claim: Pre-implantation-like gene expression was lost upon dox withdrawal and iPSC-T derivation during primed reprogramming.
source: However, such expression was lost upon dox withdrawal and iPSC-T derivation during primed reprogramming (Figure 2D) (Cacchiarelli et al., 2015)
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2D and citation to prior work.

claim: The reprogramming cells at day 20 and 24 and niPSC-Ts most closely resembled human embryos at the late blastocyst stage.
source: In addition, in comparing the transcriptional profiles between the naïve reprogramming process of hiF-Ts to niPSC-Ts and human early embryo development (Yan et al., 2013), we found that the reprogramming cells at day 20 and 24 and niPSC-Ts most closely resembled human embryos at the late blastocyst stage (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 2E and citation to embryo development data.

claim: The major wave of embryonic genome activation (EGA) occurs at approximately day three at ~8 cell stage during human embryo development.
source: During human embryo development, the major wave of embryonic genome activation (EGA) occurs at approximately day three at ~8 cell (8C) stage (Niakan et al., 2012; Vassena et al., 2011)
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research on human EGA timing.

claim: 538 genes were identified with expression levels peaking at the 8C stage during human embryonic development.
source: By analyzing single cell RNA-seq datasets of human early embryos (Yan et al., 2013), we identified 538 genes with expression levels peaking at the 8C stage during human embryonic development (Figure 3A)
evidence: Supported by analysis of single cell RNA-seq data and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 8C-genes were significantly enriched in the cluster including genes important for gamete generation.
source: Further investigation revealed that these 8C-genes were significantly enriched in the cluster including genes important for gamete generation (Fisher's exact test p-value=3.784322e-08) (Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Figure 2—figure supplement 2)
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis (p-value=3.784322e-08) and data shown in figures.

claim: 8C-genes exhibited transiently up-regulated expression patterns during the late stages of naïve reprogramming.
source: Further investigation revealed that these 8C-genes were significantly enriched in the cluster including genes important for gamete generation (Fisher's exact test p-value=3.784322e-08) (Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Figure 2—figure supplement 2) and exhibited similar transiently up-regulated expression patterns during the late stages of naïve reprogramming (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Mouse homologs of ZSCAN4 are 2C-stage restricted and are important for telomere stability in mouse ESCs and iPSCs.
source: In addition to ZSCAN4 (Figure 3C; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), whose mouse homologs are 2C-stage restricted and are important for telomere stability in mouse ESCs and iPSCs (Ko, 2016; Zalzman et al., 2010)
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research on mouse Zscan4 function.

claim: MBD3L2/3/4/5 genes are homologs of the mouse Mbd3l2 gene, which is specifically expressed at the 2C stage during mouse development.
source: More importantly, we identified MBD3L2/3/4/5 genes as 8C-genes during human embryo development (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B); these genes are the homologs of the mouse Mbd3l2 gene, which is specifically expressed at the 2C stage during mouse development (Jiang et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and citation to prior research.

claim: MBD3L2/3/4/5 showed dramatically increased expression during the late stages of naïve reprogramming from day 20 to 24 even after dox withdrawal, then decreased sharply after niPSC-T derivation.
source: Similar to the genes listed above, the transcriptional dynamics of MBD3L2/3/4/5 also showed dramatically increased expression during the late stages of naïve reprogramming from day 20 to 24 even after dox withdrawal, then decreased sharply after niPSC-T derivation (Figure 3C, D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3C, D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D.

claim: During primed reprogramming, only a small transient wave of ZSCAN4 expression was observed during the late stages from day 20 to day 24.
source: However, during the primed reprogramming, we observed only a small transient wave of ZSCAN4 expression during the late stages from day 20 to day 24 (Figure 3C)
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Only marginal MBD3L2/3/4/5 expression was observed throughout the primed reprogramming induction process.
source: and only marginal MBD3L2/3/4/5 expression throughout the induction process (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The MBD3L2/3/4/5 genes are loci-clustered in the human genome and are far from MBD3L1.
source: Interestingly, the MBD3L2/3/4/5 genes are loci-clustered in the human genome and are far from MBD3L1.
evidence: Statement about genomic organization of MBD3L genes.

claim: The amino acid sequences of each gene in the MBD3L2/3/4/5 cluster are identical.
source: Although these genes exhibited differential mRNA expression levels, the amino acid sequences of each gene in the cluster are identical
evidence: Statement about sequence identity of MBD3L genes.

claim: The MBD3L2/3/4/5 gene cluster might have evolved from mouse Mbd3l2 via the copy-paste mode.
source: thus suggesting that the gene cluster might have evolved from mouse Mbd3l2 via the copy-paste mode, similar to the situation observed in mouse Zscan4 retrotransposons and ERV repeats.
evidence: Speculative statement based on sequence similarity and genomic organization.

claim: Robust expression of ZSCAN4 and MBD3L2-5 could be observed around day 24 during naïve reprogramming.
source: Using specific human ZSCAN4 and MBD3L2-5 antibodies, we performed immunostaining in cells during reprogramming. While only weak expression of ZSCAN4 as well as no expression of MBD3L2-5 could be detected around day 14, we could observe robust expression of ZSCAN4 and MBD3L2-5 around day 24 during naïve reprogramming (Figure 3E).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Only weak expression of ZSCAN4 and no expression of MBD3L2-5 could be detected around day 14 during naïve reprogramming.
source: Using specific human ZSCAN4 and MBD3L2-5 antibodies, we performed immunostaining in cells during reprogramming. While only weak expression of ZSCAN4 as well as no expression of MBD3L2-5 could be detected around day 14, we could observe robust expression of ZSCAN4 and MBD3L2-5 around day 24 during naïve reprogramming (Figure 3E).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: MBD3L2-5 expression could not be detected during primed reprogramming process.
source: However, the expression of MBD3L2-5 could not be detected during primed reprogramming process (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: MBD3L2-5+ cells could be observed in naïve iPSC clones compared to their absence in primed iPSCs.
source: Although the transcriptional profiles of MBD3L cluster genes exhibited sharply decreased mRNA expression in the derived niPSC-T lines, we could still observe MBD3L2-5+ cells in naïve iPSC clones compared to their absence in primed iPSCs by immunostaining (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F)
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The expression of MBD3L2/3/4/5 is an indicator for naïve pluripotency.
source: suggesting the expression of MBD3L2/3/4/5 as an indicator for naïve pluripotency.
evidence: Inference based on differential expression between naïve and primed states.

claim: Transient expression of 8C-genes occurs specifically during the late stages of naïve reprogramming.
source: In summary, the transient expression of 8C-genes, which occurs specifically during the late stages of naïve reprogramming, suggests the emergence of gene network activation with 8C-stage-like characteristics.
evidence: Summary statement based on multiple lines of evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: Naïve reprogramming underwent reactivation of gene programs with human EGA-like characteristics.
source: Compared with the primed reprogramming that finally stabilized at the post-implantation-like state (Cacchiarelli et al., 2015), naïve reprogramming not only reached the pre-implantation-like status but more importantly, underwent reactivation of gene programs with human EGA-like characteristics.
evidence: Summary statement based on multiple lines of evidence and comparison to prior work.

claim: Integrants of the HERVK-family were activated upon EGA during development.
source: Notably, integrants of the HERVK-family that were activated upon EGA during development (Grow et al., 2015), especially MER9a3-HERVK9, were significantly up-regulated at day 12 of naïve reprogramming and down-regulated upon niPSC-T derivation (Figure 3I; J).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work and data shown in Figure 3I and J.

claim: MER9a3-HERVK9 was significantly up-regulated at day 12 of naïve reprogramming and down-regulated upon niPSC-T derivation.
source: Notably, integrants of the HERVK-family that were activated upon EGA during development (Grow et al., 2015), especially MER9a3-HERVK9, were significantly up-regulated at day 12 of naïve reprogramming and down-regulated upon niPSC-T derivation (Figure 3I; J).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3I and J.

claim: Transient activation of 2C-specific MERVL/ZSCAN4 transcriptional network occurs in the intermediate-late stages of mouse iPSC reprogramming.
source: These results, together with the recent observations of the transient activation of 2C-specific MERVL/ZSCAN4 transcriptional network in the intermediate-late stages of mouse iPSC reprogramming (Eckersley-Maslin et al., 2016)
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research on mouse reprogramming.

claim: Naïve human ESCs display a unique transposon signature of cleavage-stage embryos with significant overexpression of the SINE-VNTR-Alu (SVA) family of transposon elements.
source: Recent studies in naïve pluripotency evaluation have indicated that naïve human ESCs display a unique transposon signature of cleavage-stage embryos with significant overexpression of the SINE-VNTR-Alu (SVA) family of transposon elements (Theunissen et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research on naïve ESC transposon signatures.

claim: Reprogramming to naïve pluripotency induced significant up-regulation of several subgroups of the SVA family highly expressed during the morula-stage of human early embryo development, with the highest expression levels in niPSC-Ts.
source: In our system, reprogramming to naïve pluripotency induced significant up-regulation of several subgroups of the SVA family highly expressed during the morula-stage of human early embryo development, with the highest expression levels in niPSC-Ts (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: LTR7 and HERVH-int exhibited higher expression levels across primed reprogramming than across naïve induction.
source: Similar to previous observations (Theunissen et al., 2016), LTR7 and HERVH-int in the LTR7-HERVH family that were highly expressed in hESC0 and hESC10 that simulated the post-implantation stages, with no enrichment in 8C or morula stages during development (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C), exhibited higher expression levels across primed reprogramming than across naïve induction (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and 2D, and citation to prior work.

claim: A significant decrease in global DNA methylation was observed throughout the naïve pluripotency induction process.
source: In contrast to the continuous hypermethylation during primed reprogramming, a significant decrease in global DNA methylation was observed throughout the naïve pluripotency induction process (Figure 4A; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The average methylation level in niPSC-Ts resembles that in ICM.
source: including an average methylation level resembling that in ICM by the end of reprogramming in niPSC-Ts, as previously demonstrated (Figure 4A) (Leitch et al., 2013; Okae et al., 2014; Pastor et al., 2016; Smith et al., 2014; Theunissen et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4A and citations to prior research.

claim: Quantitative analysis via HPLC-MS revealed a dramatic decrease in 5mC levels throughout naïve reprogramming but not the primed reprogramming process.
source: Quantitative analysis via HPLC-MS also revealed a dramatic decrease in 5mC levels throughout naïve reprogramming but not the primed reprogramming process (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by HPLC-MS data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Naïve-specific DMRs showed a dramatic trend of down-regulation in the average methylation ratios during naïve reprogramming, but no significant changes during primed reprogramming.
source: For detailed analysis, we characterized naïve-specific differentially methylated Regions (DMRs) by comparing the DMRs of niPSC-Ts with those of hiF-Ts and piPSC-Ts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D); the results showed a dramatic trend of down-regulation in the average methylation ratios during naïve reprogramming, but no significant changes during primed reprogramming (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Naïve-specific DMRs were enriched in genes related to naïve pluripotency, which exhibited significant DNA de-methylation at the promoter regions on approximately day 24 during reprogramming.
source: We also found that the identified naïve-specific DMRs were enriched in genes related to naïve pluripotency, which exhibited significant DNA de-methylation at the promoter regions on approximately day 24 during reprogramming (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Naïve PSCs lose DNA methylation at primary imprints, which are retained throughout pre-implantation development.
source: Growing evidence indicates that naïve PSCs lose DNA methylation at primary imprints, which are retained throughout pre-implantation development (Pastor et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research.

claim: DNA methylation ratios at 31 stable primary imprints markedly decreased during naïve reprogramming, and methylation was nearly completely lost in niPSC-Ts.
source: We examined DNA methylation dynamics in 31 stable primary imprints in both the naïve and primed reprogramming processes. The DNA methylation ratios markedly decreased during naïve reprogramming, and methylation was nearly completely lost in niPSC-Ts (Figure 4D)
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: In primed reprogramming, the decrease in DNA methylation at primary imprints was more moderate, and the DNA methylation ratio finally stabilized at ~50% in piPSC-Ts.
source: However, in primed reprogramming, the decrease was more moderate, and the DNA methylation ratio finally stabilized at ~50% in piPSC-Ts, as previously reported (Figure 4D) (Pastor et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4D and citation to prior work.

claim: The failure to reactivate DNMT3A and DNMT3B, as well as the over-activation of TET2, might be causative of the genome-wide hypomethylation and loss of imprinting observed in the naïve pluripotency induction process.
source: The failure to reactivate DNMT3A and DNMT3B, as well as the over-activation of TET2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E), might be causative of the genome-wide hypomethylation and loss of imprinting observed in the naïve pluripotency induction process.
evidence: Speculative statement based on gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: There was a transient transition from H3K4me2 to H3K4me3 on the promoter regions during the naïve reprogramming process.
source: A transiently decreased pattern of 'both H3K4me2/H3K4me3' gene numbers was observed during this process, with an increasing pattern of 'H3K4me3-only' gene numbers as well as a decreasing pattern of 'H3K4me2-only' signals, thus suggesting that there was a transient transition from H3K4me2 to H3K4me3 on the promoter regions during the naïve reprogramming process (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Inference based on data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Increasing numbers of bivalent genes were observed during the naïve reprogramming process.
source: Next, we focused on H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 dynamics during reprogramming. We observed increasing numbers of bivalent genes during the reprogramming process (Figure 5A,B)
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: The up-regulation of bivalent signals was much slower with less gene numbers in niPSC-Ts during naïve reprogramming compared to primed reprogramming.
source: however, the up-regulation of bivalent signals was much slower with less gene numbers in niPSC-Ts during naïve reprogramming compared to primed reprogramming (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 5A and 5B comparing naïve and primed systems.

claim: Two clusters of genes highly related to embryonic development showed increasing bivalent signals on their promoter regions during primed reprogramming, while exhibiting almost no H3K4me3/H3K27me3 signals during the whole reprogramming process to naïve pluripotency.
source: For further comparison, we clustered the genes with similar patterns of bivalency on their promoters in both naïve and primed reprogramming process, and found that there were two clusters of genes highly related to embryonic development showing increasing bivalent signals on their promoter regions during primed reprogramming, while exhibiting almost no H3K4me3/H3K27me3 signals during the whole reprogramming process to naïve pluripotency (Figure 5C; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, consistent with prior reports.

claim: The average H3K4me3 signals were highly correlated with the transcriptional dynamics and increased around the TSSs of genes with pre-implantation and early embryogenesis signatures.
source: To address the effect of histone modification on transcriptional activity, we also examined the H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 modification dynamics around the transcription start sites (TSSs) of gene clusters with different expression patterns. The average H3K4me3 signals were highly correlated with the transcriptional dynamics and increased around the TSSs of genes with pre-implantation and early embryogenesis signatures, while the average H3K27me3 signals decreased around the TSSs of these genes during reprogramming (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: A decreasing pattern of H3K9me3 signals was observed during naïve reprogramming, including integrants of SVA family.

claim: The H3K9me3 signals around the 8C-TEs, especially MER9a3-HERVK9, exhibited a transiently decreased pattern at day 14, strongly correlated with the transiently increasing transcriptional activity of these 8C-TEs during naïve reprogramming.
source: Moreover, the H3K9me3 signals around the 8C-TEs, especially MER9a3-HERVK9, exhibited a transiently decreased pattern at day 14, strongly correlated with the transiently increasing transcriptional activity of these 8C-TEs during naïve reprogramming (Figure 5F).

claim: The transcriptional levels of genes with early/late somatic, early embryogenesis- and pre-implantation-like signatures were closely correlated with the changes in epigenetic modifications at the promoter regions during naïve reprogramming.
source: Next, we focused on the down- and up-regulated patterns of genes with early/late somatic, early embryogenesis- and pre-implantation-like signatures (Figure 2C; Figure 2—figure supplement 2) and analyzed the relationships among the gene expression patterns, DNA methylation status and histone modifications. Despite their distinct expression dynamics, the transcriptional levels of these genes were closely correlated with the changes in epigenetic modifications at the promoter regions during naïve reprogramming, regulated by DNA methylation, histone modifications, or both (Figure 6A).
evidence: Supported by integrative analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Genes with higher CpG-densities in their promoters tended to undergo more rapid DNA demethylation and re-establishment of active histone modifications (H3K4me2/3), as well as earlier up-regulation in transcription during naïve reprogramming.
source: Furthermore, compared with the genes with lower CpG-densities in their promoters, genes with higher CpG-densities tended to undergo more rapid DNA demethylation and re-establishment of active histone modifications (H3K4me2/3), as well as earlier up-regulation in transcription during naïve reprogramming (Figure 6B; Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The genes associated with core naïve pluripotency were enriched primarily in the LCP and ICP groups.
source: We examined the genes classified by different CpG-densities at promoter regions and found that the genes associated with core naïve pluripotency were enriched primarily in the LCP and ICP groups (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The transcriptional dynamics strongly correlated with epigenetic changes during naïve reprogramming, which may be affected by the CpG density at gene promoter regions.
source: Together, these results indicated that the transcriptional dynamics strongly correlated with epigenetic changes during naïve reprogramming, which may be affected by the CpG density at gene promoter regions.
evidence: Summary statement based on integrative analysis of transcriptional and epigenetic data.

claim: Integrative analysis of transcriptional and epigenetic dynamics across the transition from human fibroblasts to naïve iPSCs revealed ordered waves of gene network activation sharing signatures with those found during embryonic development from late embryogenesis to pre-implantation stages.
source: Using the human inducible reprogramming system together with the 5iLAF naïve induction strategy, integrative analysis of transcriptional and epigenetic dynamics across the transition from human fibroblasts to naïve iPSCs revealed ordered waves of gene network activation sharing signatures with those found during embryonic development from late embryogenesis to pre-implantation stages.
evidence: Summary statement from the abstract based on multiple lines of evidence presented in the manuscript.
